title: Singapore Retail Merchandising and Pricing
thesis: On one governed platform, Snowflake turns daily merchandise line activity from Tembusu Fresh Mart, a fictional Singapore supermarket chain, into price integrity KPIs, 7-day unplanned-markdown risk per line, markdown depth anomalies and AI answers that cite their sources.

talking_points: 48 merchandise lines are ranged in the store clusters of five HDB towns: Bukit Batok, Sengkang, Toa Payoh, Bedok and Yishun. The cards show price integrity rate, pricing exceptions, unplanned markdowns and net sales in SGD.
Each KPI is computed as a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so you can trace it to line-day rows.

The exception-type chart separates exceptions that end in an unplanned markdown from ones that always get resolved, such as the town-wide competitor price campaigns in Sengkang and Yishun, answered with a price match.
tabs.call_out: Merchandising KPIs you can trace to source rows

transition.line: Which lines need a pricing review first?

talking_points: A Snowflake ML classifier estimates, per merchandise line, the chance of an unplanned markdown in the next 7 days.
Precision and recall come from the latest 14 days held out of training, shown next to the base rate.
Anomaly detection picks out unusual markdown depth, and the forecast covers the next 14 days of pricing exceptions.
tabs.call_out: ML that is evaluated honestly, next to the data

transition.line: Are price audits and supplier funding agreements up to date?

talking_points: Price audit compliance, supplier funding agreement coverage and pending agreements show where pricing controls are slipping.
Plotting price audit compliance against unplanned markdowns per line shows where the two move together; it is an association in synthetic data, not proof of cause.
The action memo is drafted only from KPI, line, exception-type and risk rows, and a person reviews it before anything is sent.
show: Price audit compliance vs unplanned markdowns
tabs.call_out: Controls and a reviewed memo, from the same data

transition.line: What is happening at the registers right now?

talking_points: New POS events arrive in RAW.LIVE_POS, either from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The alert records each EXCEPTION event with an SOP hint and the line's risk band, then emails the on-call pricing analyst, so a mismatch at a heartland outlet becomes a pricing case the same day.
tabs.call_out: From a live pricing exception to a pricing case on one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers metric questions with Cortex Analyst over the semantic view, and procedure questions with Cortex Search over 14 synthetic SOPs.
Every answer shows the SQL it generated and the SOP IDs it cited.
tabs.call_out: Answers in plain language that you can check

transition.line: This is how it fits together.

talking_points: One core supports two builds: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake with Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q.
All data shown is synthetic and rebuilds the same way from the repo.
tabs.call_out: A governed core with an optional AWS edge
